jobs.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: one transparent standalone isometric strategy-game animation sprite, NOT a sheet. Input image is the approved Ruan Xiaoqi four-direction contact-A atlas: it is the identity, clothing, spear, palette, lighting, proportion and camera reference. Produce exactly ONE full-body REAR THREE-QUARTER figure of this same rugged adult Chinese fisherman, keeping the weathered green conical woven reed hat, layered short green straw rain cape, raw pale linen waist wrap, rolled grey trousers and bare feet. He carries exactly ONE plain thin brown spear with a small iron leaf point, low in his RIGHT hand. No extra rod on his back. Native crisp hand-painted game rendering and alpha transparency, no shadow, text, grid, ground or effects. Keep whole hat, spear and every toe inside generous 8% clear outer margin. This is the OPPOSITE CONTACT step of a normal walk, NOT idle or a mirrored copy: redraw the anatomy and cloth below the belt so the legs exchange which is leading and trailing, while the upper body keeps the same direction and scale. Natural two knees/two ankles/two feet only. The far foot is visibly higher on the image and planted ahead, the trailing near heel is visibly lower on the image and lifted with toes still touching. Strong vertical separation between the two feet is essential. No armor, boots, trident, water magic, gods, crowns or weapons added. The precise gait is conservative animation design, not a claimed novel event. DIRECTION: rear view facing diagonally UP and to the RIGHT (NE), so only the right edge of his face is visible under the hat. Gait B: his LEFT leg (on the LEFT of the pelvis in this rear view) is now the FORWARD weight-bearing leg: thigh and shin extend away/up-right, left foot planted around 78% of image height with toes pointing up-right. His RIGHT leg on the RIGHT is now trailing back/down toward the viewer, knee slightly flexed, heel lifted, right toes contact around 89% height and sole partly visible. Reference contact A instead has its left foot back and right foot ahead; EXCHANGE this leg depth clearly. Keep the spear in the same RIGHT hand on screen right, tip pointing down-right, spatially separate from both feet. The cape covers upper thighs but does NOT hide either knee, shin or foot.
